_note: Seed list of physics schools, defined by founders. Members are the founders plus all their recorded academic descendants. These are conventional textbook groupings, not settled facts: edit, add or remove freely, then run LINEAGE_FIELD=physics scripts/export_context.py. Person ids are Academic Family Tree pids (see the explorer URL #/p/<pid>).

schools.name: Cavendish Laboratory
schools.note: J. J. Thomson and Rutherford at Cambridge: the electron, the nucleus, experimental atomic physics.

schools.name: Sommerfeld school
schools.note: Arnold Sommerfeld in Munich: atomic theory; students include Heisenberg, Pauli, Debye and Bethe.

schools.name: Copenhagen school
schools.note: Niels Bohr's institute: the Copenhagen interpretation of quantum mechanics.

schools.name: Göttingen quantum mechanics
schools.note: Max Born in Göttingen: matrix mechanics and the statistical interpretation.

schools.name: Leiden school
schools.note: Paul Ehrenfest in Leiden: statistical physics and early quantum theory.

schools.name: Soviet theoretical physics
schools.note: Landau and Tamm in Moscow: the Landau school and the Lebedev theory group.

schools.name: Berkeley Radiation Laboratory
schools.note: Oppenheimer's theory group and Lawrence's cyclotron lab.

schools.name: Fermi school
schools.note: Enrico Fermi in Rome and Chicago: nuclear and particle physics.

schools.name: Cornell nuclear theory
schools.note: Hans Bethe at Cornell: nuclear physics and astrophysics.

schools.name: Wheeler school
schools.note: John Wheeler at Princeton and Texas: relativity, gravitation, Feynman and Thorne.

schools.name: Columbia and Harvard QED
schools.note: Rabi's molecular beams at Columbia and Schwinger's quantum electrodynamics at Harvard.

schools.name: Princeton solid state
schools.note: Eugene Wigner at Princeton: symmetry, nuclear and solid-state theory (Bardeen, Seitz).
